correctness.rationale: For every mixed binary input BWT begins with one and has k ones, giving at most 2k runs. A gap-length t bucket contributes a marked one exactly at t=g_i; pairwise separation by at least two yields isolating zero buckets, and positive gaps force trailing BWT zero, giving 2k. Sorted gap lists are partitions of n−k(k+1) into at most k parts and have k! orderings/k rootings per primitive necklace. Uniform weak-composition gap sampling and a union bound prove the k²(k−1)/(n−1) failure bound. Exhaustive and independent gap checks support but do not replace these arguments.

value.rationale: The BWT run count controls compressed indexing and RLE storage; sharp maximal-run behavior within a sparse fixed-weight population is natural and contrasts with usual clustering. This produces a structural gap certificate, exact all-parameter primitive-necklace population count, and an all-growing-weight probability-one result rather than a mere isolated example or a small enumerated slice. Its explicit sufficiency window exposes a quantitative sparse-to-denser transition to investigate.
